title: Global Theme configuration change in plasmoidsetupscripts for org.kde.plasma.battery no longer changes percentage indicator
line: A global theme's widget setup scripts now apply to widgets in the System Tray again, such as showing the battery percentage.
explanation: Plasmashell runs a global theme's plasmoidsetupscripts from the appletCreated signal of every containment the corona tracks. Since libplasma's nested containments (3ad38c16, Plasma 6.4), the System Tray is a containment inside the panel instead of a top-level one, so the corona never hooked it and scripts for tray applets like the battery never ran. The change also connects the setup scripts for nested containments as they are added to a containment, before they create their applets.

commits.message:
shell: run plasmoid setup scripts for applets in the System Tray

Since the System Tray became a nested containment, the corona no longer
tracks it, so a global theme's plasmoidsetupscripts never ran for the
applets it creates. Also hook the scripts up for nested containments.

BUG: 513669

media.caption: Master, after applying a theme whose setup script enables the battery percentage: no percentage in the tray
With the fix, same steps: the tray's battery shows its percentage

reviews.text: Clean fix at the right layer: since libplasma made System Tray a nested containment, ShellCorona::handleContainmentAdded no longer saw it, so hooking appletCreated recursively via appletAboutToBeAdded restores plasmoidsetupscripts before nested containments create their default applets. Verified with both a control clock script and the reporter's battery showPercentage script, and confirmed restored tray applets do not re-run setup scripts on restart. Minor nitpick: moving a nested containment between containments could attach a duplicate lambda connection, though setup scripts are idempotent in practice.
